es.q: Explain the key promoter elements in prokaryotic genes and their crucial role in initiating transcription, referencing specific sequences mentioned in the article.
es.m: In prokaryotic genes, promoter regions are crucial upstream sequences responsible for initiating transcription by recruiting RNA polymerase. They are typically located 50–100 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site (+1). Key sequences within prokaryotic promoters include: 1. **Pribnow Box (-10 Sequence)**: This sequence, typically TATAAT, is located around 10 base pairs upstream of the transcription start site and aids in RNA polymerase binding to the DNA. 2. **-35 Sequence**: Located approximately 35 base pairs upstream, this sequence (TTGACA) is recognized by sigma factors during the initiation of transcription, guiding RNA polymerase to the correct start site.
